docs.title: Star-Allele-Search
docs.text:
Figure 1. Star-Allele-Search homepage.

Welcome to the Star-Allele-Search documentation.

Star-Allele-Search is a pharmacogenomics application designed to retrieve, validate and annotate pharmacogenomic star alleles using information from PharmVar, ClinPGx and CPIC resources. The software provides researchers, clinical scientists and healthcare professionals with a simple interface for exploring pharmacogenomic alleles, associated phenotypes and clinical guidance.

docs.title: What is a Star Allele?
docs.text:
Many pharmacogenomic genes are described using star allele nomenclature rather than individual sequence variants.

Examples include:

CYP2C19*2
CYP2D6*4
TPMT*3A
SLCO1B1*5

A star allele represents a group of genetic variants that are inherited together as a haplotype and have a known impact on drug response. Star alleles are widely used in pharmacogenomics because they provide a concise and clinically meaningful way to describe pharmacogenetic variation.

For example, CYP2C19*2 is associated with reduced enzyme activity and can influence response to medications such as clopidogrel.

docs.title: PharmVar
docs.text: The Pharmacogene Variation Consortium (PharmVar) is a centralised repository of pharmacogene variation data and star allele nomenclature. PharmVar provides definitions for core alleles, sub-alleles, functional annotations and stable PharmVar identifiers (PVIDs).

docs.title: ClinPGx
docs.text: ClinPGx is a comprehensive resource supporting the clinical implementation of pharmacogenomics and provides information on genes, alleles, phenotypes and guideline annotations.

docs.title: CPIC
docs.text: The Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium (CPIC) publishes evidence-based pharmacogenomic prescribing guidelines that help healthcare professionals understand how genetic variation may affect drug response.

docs.title: Clinical Interpretation
docs.text: Retrieve pharmacogenomic information for clinically relevant genes and alleles to support interpretation of genetic test results.

docs.title: Research
docs.text: Explore allele definitions and clinical annotations for pharmacogenomics research and method development.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Verify allele nomenclature and compare information across multiple pharmacogenomic resources.

docs.text: Learn about star allele nomenclature, diplotypes and pharmacogenomic phenotypes.

docs.title: New to Pharmacogenomics?
docs.text:
If you are unfamiliar with pharmacogenomic terminology, the following concepts may be useful:

  • Star alleles
  • Core alleles
  • Sub-alleles
  • Diplotypes
  • Phenotypes
  • Pharmacogenomic prescribing guidelines

The User Guide contains additional examples and background information to help new users understand these concepts.

docs.title: Local Installation
docs.text: This guide explains how to install and run Star-Allele-Search in a local development environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Ensure the following software is installed:

  • Python 3.12
  • Git
  • Conda (recommended)

Verify your installation:

python --version
git --version
conda --version

docs.title: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Clone the repository and move into the project directory:

git clone https://github.com/dianaivanoiu/Star-Allele-Search.git
cd Star-Allele-Search

docs.title: Create the Conda Environment
docs.text:
Star-Allele-Search provides an environment configuration file to ensure reproducible installation.

Create the environment:

conda env create -f environment.yaml

Activate the environment:

conda activate Star-allele-search

docs.title: Install Project Dependencies
docs.text:
Install the package in the current environment:

pip install .

The installation uses the project configuration defined in:

pyproject.toml

Dependencies are automatically loaded from:

requirements.txt

docs.title: Configure Environment Variables
docs.text:
Several external services require authentication credentials.

Create a file called:

.env

in the project root directory.

Example:

PHARMVAR_API_KEY=your_pharmvar_api_key

TERRACIPHER_EMAIL=your_email@example.com
TERRACIPHER_PASSWORD=your_password

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Variable Purpose PHARMVAR_API_KEY Access to the PharmVar API TERRACIPHER_EMAIL TerraCipher login email TERRACIPHER_PASSWORD TerraCipher login password

The application automatically loads these values using the python-dotenv package.

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Confirm that the package can be imported successfully:

python

import star_allele_search

Exit Python:

exit()

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
Execute the automated test suite:

pytest

Run tests with coverage analysis:

pytest --cov=App --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html

Coverage reports will be written to:

htmlcov/

docs.title: Missing PharmVar API Key
docs.text:
Example error:

401 Unauthorized

Verify:

PHARMVAR_API_KEY

has been configured correctly in the .env file.

docs.title: Missing TerraCipher Credentials
docs.text:
Example error:

Please set login details to terra

Verify:

TERRACIPHER_EMAIL
TERRACIPHER_PASSWORD

are present in the .env file.

docs.title: Dependency Installation Issues
docs.text:
Upgrade pip and reinstall dependencies:

pip install --upgrade pip
pip install .

docs.title: Installed Package Structure
docs.text:
The project is packaged as:

star_allele_search

and is built using modern Python packaging through:

pyproject.toml

This allows installation using:

pip install .

which provides a reproducible environment across development platforms.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Star-Allele-Search is a pharmacogenomics application developed to retrieve, validate and annotate pharmacogenomic star allele information.

The application integrates information from multiple external resources, including PharmVar, ClinPGx, HGNC and VariantValidator, to provide allele-specific information, phenotype annotations and clinical guideline recommendations.

docs.text:
The software follows a modular architecture.

 ClinPGx Annotation Retrieval
          │
          ▼
 Guideline Processing
          │
          ▼

The application integrates with the following external resources:

  • PharmVar
  • ClinPGx
  • HGNC
  • VariantValidator
  • TerraCipher

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Star-Allele-Search uses automated testing to verify that application functionality behaves as expected and to reduce the risk of introducing regressions during development.

Testing is performed using PyTest and is automatically executed through GitHub Actions whenever code is pushed to the repository or submitted in a pull request.

docs.title: Automated Testing
docs.text:
The automated test suite verifies the behaviour of individual modules and application workflows.

Tests can be executed locally using:

pytest

Figure 1. Successful execution of the Star-Allele-Search test suite.

docs.title: Test Coverage
docs.text:
Coverage analysis is performed using pytest-cov to measure how much of the source code is exercised by the automated tests.

Coverage can be generated using:

pytest --cov=App --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html -vv

The command generates a terminal summary and an HTML coverage report that can be inspected in a web browser.

Figure 2. Coverage generation using pytest-cov.

docs.title: Coverage Objectives
docs.text:
The test suite is designed to cover:

  • PharmVar API integration
  • ClinPGx annotation retrieval
  • HGNC identifier retrieval
  • Guideline processing
  • Variant validation
  • Exception handling
  • Error conditions

docs.title: Unit Testing
docs.text:
Unit tests validate individual functions in isolation to ensure that each software component behaves correctly.

Examples include:

  • PharmVar data retrieval functions
  • HGNC lookup functions
  • Annotation filtering functions
  • Guideline catalogue generation

docs.title: Exception Testing
docs.text:
Exception tests ensure that the software handles invalid data and external service failures appropriately.

Examples include:

  • Invalid allele names
  • Network failures
  • Missing API credentials tinuous Integration

Star-Allele-Search uses GitHub Actions for Continuous Integration (CI).

Every push and pull request automatically triggers a workflow that:

  1. Creates a clean Python environment.
  2. Installs project dependencies.
  3. Executes the automated test suite.
  4. Generates code coverage metrics.
  5. Uploads coverage reports to Codecov.

This ensures that code changes are automatically validated before being merged into the project.

../images/github_actions_passing.png

Figure 3. Successful GitHub Actions workflow showing automated testing and Codecov integration.

Star-Allele-Search is a pharmacogenomics application that retrieves, validates and annotates star allele information from multiple external resources.

Figure 1. Homepage

The application combines information from:

  • PharmVar
  • ClinPGx

  • DPWG

to provide clinically relevant pharmacogenomic information.

docs.title: Understanding Star Alleles and Diplotypes
docs.text:
Pharmacogenomic results are often reported using star allele nomenclature.

A diplotype consists of two star alleles inherited from the two parental chromosomes.

For example:

  • Gene: CYP2C19
  • Allele 1: *17
  • Allele 2: *17
  • Diplotype: CYP2C19 17/17

Figure 2. Example star allele.

The figure below illustrates how a diplotype is represented.

Figure 3. Example pharmacogenomic diplotype notation.

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
The user provides a star allele query.

CYP2C19*2

The application:

  1. Retrieves allele information from PharmVar.
  2. Validates gene and allele information.
  3. Retrieves phenotype information.
  4. Retrieves associated pharmacogenomic guidelines.
  5. Generates an annotated result.
User Input
     │
     ▼
 Star Allele Query
     │
     ▼
 PharmVar Retrieval
     │
     ▼
 Phenotype Mapping
     │
     ▼
 Guideline Retrieval
     │
     ▼
 Results

docs.title: Example Search
docs.text:
The following example shows a search for CYP2C19*2(UPDATE CLOSER TO SUBMISSION).

Figure 4. Example search for CYP2C19*2.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
CYP2C19*2

The query should contain:

  • A valid gene name
  • A valid star allele designation

Example valid inputs:

CYP2C19*2
CYP2D6*4
SLCO1B1*5
TPMT*3A

docs.title: Understanding the Results
docs.text: The application may return several categories of information.

docs.title: Star Allele Information
docs.text:
Example:

Gene: CYP2C19
Allele: *2
Function: No Function

This information is retrieved from PharmVar.

docs.title: Phenotype Information
docs.text:
Example:

Phenotype:
Poor Metaboliser

Phenotype predictions are generated from available pharmacogenomic annotations.

docs.title: Clinical Guidelines
docs.text:
The application retrieves available recommendations from sources such as:

  • CPIC
  • DPWG

Example:

Drug: Clopidogrel

Recommendation:
Consider an alternative antiplatelet agent in patients with reduced CYP2C19 function.

docs.title: Clinical Interpretation
docs.text:
The application can be used to identify clinical recommendations associated with pharmacogenomic variants.

Examples:

  • Clopidogrel and CYP2C19
  • Simvastatin and SLCO1B1
  • Thiopurines and TPMT

docs.title: Research and Validation
docs.text:
Researchers can use the software to:

  • Validate allele nomenclature
  • Retrieve allele definitions
  • Compare annotations across resources
  • Review published recommendations

docs.title: Allele Not Found
docs.text:
Example:

No results returned

Possible causes:

  • Incorrect gene symbol
  • Incorrect star allele designation
  • Allele not present in the data source

Verify the allele using PharmVar.

docs.title: API Connection Errors
docs.text:
Example:

Failed to retrieve PharmVar data

Possible causes:

  • Network connectivity problems
  • Invalid API credentials
  • Temporary service outage

Check internet connectivity and API configuration.
